chunks: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated: I was with Abu Ja'far (the second Imam, peace be upon him) when Salah ibn Muhammad ibn Sahl entered upon him (and he managed the endowment for him in Qum). He said: 'O my master, make me free from the ten thousand dirhams, for I have spent them.' He said to him: 'You are free.' When Salah left, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'One of them jumps upon the wealth of the Family of Muhammad, their orphans, their poor, and their travelers, takes it, then comes and says: 'Make me free.' Do you think he believed that I would say 'No, do not do it'? By God, God Almighty will question them about that on the Day of Judgment with a sharp questioning.'

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: Know, may God guide you, that the leniency mentioned in this chapter regarding consuming khums by spending it was specifically revealed for marriages, for the reason previously mentioned in the traditions from the Imams (peace be upon them), so that the offspring of their Shias may be pure. It was not revealed for wealth, and what I delayed from the preceding matters regarding the strictness in khums and its exclusive right belongs to wealth.

This statement is indicated by what he narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him, and I read his letter to him on the way to Mecca. He said: 'What I made obligatory upon you in this year, which is the year of twenty and two hundred, is only for a meaning among meanings which I dislike to explain fully for fear of dissemination. And I will explain part of it to you, if God wills. Indeed, my clients, I ask God for their rectification, or some of them, fell short in what was obligatory upon them, so I knew that and loved to purify and purify them with what I did in my year regarding the matter of khums.'

God Almighty said: 'Take charity from their wealth to purify them and to make them grow in purity, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a comfort to them, and God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.' Have they not known that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities, and that it is God who is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful? And say: 'Work, for God will see your work, and His Messenger, and the believers, and you will be returned to the Knower of the Unseen and the Seen, and He will inform you about what you used to do.'

And I did not make that obligatory upon them every year, nor do I make obligatory upon them except the zakat which God prescribed upon them. And I made khums obligatory upon them in this year only in gold and silver upon which the year has passed. And I did not make that obligatory upon them in movable goods, vessels, animals, servants, profit earned in trade, or estates, except an estate which I will explain to you, as a lightening from me upon my clients and a favor from me upon them for what the Sultan seizes from their wealth and what befalls them in their own selves.

As for the spoils and benefits, they are obligatory upon them every year. God Almighty said: 'And know that whatever you gain of spoils, then for God is one fifth of it and for the Messenger and for the relatives and the orphans and the poor and the traveler, if you believe in God and in what We sent down to Our servant on the day of criterion - the day when the two armies met, and God is over all things omnipotent.'

And the spoils and benefits, may God have mercy on you, are: the spoil that a man gains, the benefit that he acquires, the gift from a man to a man which has great significance, and the inheritance that is not calculated from a non-father or non-son, and like an enemy whose property is seized, so his wealth is taken, and like wealth that is taken whose owner is not known. And from the type of what came to some of my clients from the wealth of the Khurramites, the impious, I have known that great wealth came to some of my clients. So whoever has something of that, let him send it to my agent, and whoever is distant and far from the journey, let him intend to send it, even after a while, for the intention of the believer is better than his action.

As for what I make obligatory from the crops and estates every year, it is half of the sixth (one-twelfth) for whoever's estate sustains his livelihood, and for whoever's estate does not sustain his livelihood, there is no half sixth upon him nor anything else.' If a questioner says: 'If the matter regarding the wealth of people is as you mentioned regarding the obligation of khums in it, and in the spoils what you described regarding the obligation of paying khums from it, and the ruling of the lands is as you clarified regarding the obligation of exclusive management by the Imams (peace be upon them), either because they have exclusive right to their necks (ownership) other than the people, like the anfal, and the lands whose people vacate them, or for the obligation of management in them by taking the khums and guaranteeing it for them, like the land of khraj and what runs in its manner, then it should be that no marriage is permissible for you, no trade is cleared for you, and no food is suitable for you in any way or from any reason.'

It was said to him: 'Indeed, the matter, although it is as you mentioned regarding the question of the exclusive management of the Imams (peace be upon them) in these things, then we have a way to escape from what you obligated upon us. As for the spoils, trades, marriages, and what runs in their manner from what khums is obligatory for the Imam in it, then they (peace be upon them) have made it permissible for us and validated for us the management in it. And we have preceded that in what passed, and it is also confirmed by what he narrated:'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between wealth subject to khums and items where the Imam has exclusive rights according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this narration by distinguishing between the general permissibility of consuming khums for marriages and trade (a specific concession to purify the faithful) and the stricter obligation on specific assets like gold, silver, and agricultural produce. The text highlights the Imam's discretionary authority to impose khums temporarily to cleanse the wealth of his followers from the Sultan's exactions, while clarifying that exclusive rights to certain lands remain with the Imam, yet the faithful are granted flexibility in utilizing their earnings.
